summary: Pan-Asianism holds that the peoples of Asia share a common civilization and heritage and should stand together, in cooperation or political unity, against Western imperialism and colonial domination. It arose in the late 19th century among Japanese, Chinese, Indian and other thinkers. Its Japanese strand increasingly claimed Japanese leadership of Asia and ended as the justification of the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, while Sun Yat-sen's 1924 Greater Asianism called for a moral union of equals against the Western rule of might.
scope: The classical Pan-Asianism of c. 1850 to 1945, as Saaler and Szpilman's overview and the two reviews of the field describe it: a loose cluster of ideas about Asian identity and solidarity with no fixed programme, covering its cooperative strand (Okakura Tenshin's 'Asia is one', Tagore, Taraknath Das, Sun Yat-sen's 1924 Greater Asianism speech) and its Japanese leadership strand (Konoe Fumimaro, Kita Ikki, Ōkawa Shūmei, the Asian Monroe Doctrine claims of the 1930s). Sources name the wartime Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere as the end point of the Japanese strand but give no separate text of its own, so the 1943 conference declaration is not used. Asian values, which Saaler and Szpilman treat as a later echo, has its own catalog entry and is left out, as are the books on the local list (art, archaeology and a social-work handbook that merely contain 'Pan Asian', and an OCR-garbled 1941 Japanese conference record).

notes: Sun's 1897 Kidnapped in London is a narrative of his abduction and says nothing of Pan-Asianism, and the Marathi Gitanjali scan is unreadable OCR, so neither is cited. Asian values (a later echo in Saaler and Szpilman) is excluded from scope, so statements on Western institutions and civilizations' political forms stay null; leadership-of-a-dominant-power and sacred-emperor claims belong to the Japanese strand only and Sun's speech is silent on them. Okakura's Awakening of the East is named only once by the sources, so it is not a key work.
